requirement:
A record MUST be changed only if every rewrite a mapping calls for in it
verifies under {cite}`requirements.refactor.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.definition_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.subject_text`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.reference_digest`; otherwise the whole record MUST
be left unchanged and reported with the check that failed. Records that no
mapping affects MUST be left byte-identical.
rationale:
I found no gap. `requirements.refactor.whole_record` is carried out by `src/refactor.rs#fn[rewrite_record]`, which carries the `{impl}` reference. The obligations and their code are below.

**Obligations and code**
- **Change a record only if every rewrite the mappings call for verifies.** `rewrite_record` works on a clone of the record and collects `failures` from each check. These checks run in it or in code it reaches:
  - Definition and example records: the mapped-back body check against the recorded `requirement` or `example` field (`subject_text`), and the reference-digest check through `States::digests` (`reference_digest`).
  - Citation and site records: the item's `inputs` pass through `rewrite_input`, which does the outline-hash check (`outline_inputs`) and the requirements/definition check (`definition_inputs`). The citation equivalence check `same_citations` also runs.
  - Site records have no body field. `sites::validate_review` requires a site review's inputs to include a requirements input for the declaration of its requirement. `rewrite_input` therefore covers the body check for the site's `requirement` field.
- **Otherwise leave the whole record unchanged and report the failed check.** If `failures` is non-empty, `rewrite_record` returns `Outcome::Unchanged(failures.join("; "))`. The partially rewritten `value` is discarded, so no rewrite is partially applied. `fn[refactor]` collects these outcomes and lists them under "records unchanged". Each reason names the check that failed, for example "requirement text of X changed", "the reference set of X changed", or "inputs[i]: … no longer has the recorded hash".
- **Leave records no mapping affects byte-identical.** `rewrite_record` returns `Outcome::Unaffected` when `changed` is false. `refactor` writes only records in `Changed`, so unaffected records are never rewritten.

**Tests** (each carries a `{test}` reference to the subject)
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` asserts that the unaffected `rules.check` record is byte-identical and that it is absent from the report.
- `fn[a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale]` covers an outline-hash failure. The record is byte-identical afterwards and the report names the failed check.
- `fn[a_requirement_edited_while_moving_keeps_its_old_record]` covers a subject-text failure. The record is unchanged and no new file is created.
- `fn[a_reference_set_changed_beyond_the_mapping_blocks_every_rewrite]` covers a digest failure when the text and requirements-input rewrites would otherwise verify. It asserts that nothing is rewritten and that only the reference-set failure is reported.
- `fn[a_term_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_definition_input_stale]` covers a definition-input failure.
- `fn[a_changed_reference_set_is_reported_on_a_record_reading_nothing_moved]` covers a digest failure on a record that reads nothing moved.
- `fn[a_citation_review_whose_citations_changed_in_the_move_is_left_unchanged]` covers the citation-review check.

Together these cover the all-or-nothing behaviour, the reporting of the failed check, and the byte-identical case.
